body: This is likely a consequence of https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/47502, which has made many JSON serializations change to floats. Remember that JSON only has a `number` type, no actual `float` or `int` type; see https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/61464 and https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/101274.

> This is likely a consequence of https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/47502

Can confirm that this is indeed the first "bad" commit.

> but the DAP spec says it should be an integer.

Where are you taking that from? I only find it being typed as `number` which is a floating point number type. Json has no integer type.

> It parses JSON and puts the data into `params` dictionary. This JSON contains `seq` key which gets deserialized as a float (even though the number appears to be an integer, is this expected behavior?).

It is, we parse all numbers from json as floats. Json has no integers. It makes sense to type this as an integer in ZED for technical reasons, but we have no reason to convert this. If the Json parser used by ZED relies on non standard conventions to parse integers it is certainly not the right tool to use in the context of an open json based ecosystem.

> With this change everything works as expected. Is this something that should be fixed on server side (Godot) or client side (Zed editor)?

Both. We had the same problem with LSP and added a fix on our side since it does not add much complexity. That being said this fix is a courtesy towards non-compliant clients. If ZED tries to be a broadly compatible code editor a fix to become spec compliant on their side is required as well (and more important than us accounting for such clients).

> Where are you taking that from? I only find it being typed as number which is a floating point number type.

https://github.com/microsoft/debug-adapter-protocol/blob/fd7088dac1cf12b2741c3fa2218aed471321ab7d/debugAdapterProtocol.json#L15-L18

And in [overview.md](https://github.com/microsoft/debug-adapter-protocol/blob/main/overview.md)

> `integer`s defined in the protocol (JSON schema type `integer`) may be represented as 32 bit signed integers, although some properties disallow negative values. `number`s in the protocol (JSON schema type `number`) may be represented as 64 bit floating point numbers.

Am I reading it wrong?

That's interesting, there seems to be a disparity between the schema and the specification hosted at https://microsoft.github.io/debug-adapter-protocol/specification.html

But it doesn't matter anyway. `1.0` is still a valid integer according to json schema: https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/numeric#integer

> > `integer`s defined in the protocol (JSON schema type `integer`) may be represented as 32 bit signed integers, although some properties disallow negative values. `number`s in the protocol (JSON schema type `number`) may be represented as 64 bit floating point numbers.
> 
> Am I reading it wrong?

Assuming this document is normative for DAP and assuming DAP is written with [RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119) this is optional and does not require us to store `req` in any specific way. Even if so it makes no statement about serialization: `1.0` would still be legal json serialization of an 32bit signed integer.

> That's interesting, there seems to be a disparity between the schema and the specification hosted at https://microsoft.github.io/debug-adapter-protocol/specification.html

There was an issue, but it was closed even though it wasn't fixed https://github.com/microsoft/debug-adapter-protocol/issues/90

> Assuming this document is normative for DAP and assuming DAP is written with [RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119) this is optional and does not require us to store req in any specific way. Even if so it makes no statement about serialization: 1.0 would still be legal json serialization of an 32bit signed integer.

I understand. I will open an issue in Zed's repo later.

I'm a bit confused as to why there is an argument here. Indeed, JSON's `number` type is only a float. But also, the DAP specification is more than just JSON, and it clearly says it should be an integer. Even if we argue that Zed should accept `1.0` because it's identical from a JSON perspective, it would still be better for Godot to omit the `.0` for properties that are integers by specification, even if just for the sake of improving human readability and debuggability of the JSON.

I would implement @fstxz's suggested change (cast to int before assigning to `request_seq`). This would also have the benefit that the in-memory `Dictionary response` will have the correct Godot data type (`Variant::INT`).

Not sure if we are on the same page. I'm not against adding such a change to Godot. I'm just making the point that our current behavior is legal and thus an issue should be reported to Zed as well.

I'm totally in favor of adding this int cast on our side as well.
